decisions.reason: As a modular continuation of the already proven BASIC 518, it likely retains strong option value and low withdrawal pressure in this firm's long-cycle machinery portfolio.
A multi-model mobile shredder line with a dedicated market presence fits the firm's core mobile processing business, so management would usually continue learning rather than exit.
Although its market validation is less visible, the mobile high-speed grinder remains close to existing capabilities and is still worth keeping open as an adjacent option.
The stationary electric fine shredder is more niche and somewhat more uncertain, but its fit with tougher-processing and resource-saving trends makes continued retention plausible.
The green-waste mobile grinder serves a recognizable customer segment within the firm's installed markets, so the firm would likely keep it available while demand develops.
A dedicated page and a full line of stationary single-shaft pre-shredders indicate a substantial commitment, making near-term withdrawal relatively unlikely.
